mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in PARKS mobility over the last four weeks, driven by seasonal changes towards colder weather and shorter days, will cause a redirection of leisure activities towards indoor retail and recreation, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days, despite the continued decline in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in workplace attendance, evidenced by WORKPLACES mobility rising above -30% and holding, will increase weekday footfall in commercial areas, thereby boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -30% and stays above for at least 2 consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility rises above -30% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not improve relative to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A synergistic increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, indicating a stronger return to daily commuting and urban activity, will drive higher RETAIL_REC as more people are present in commercial and leisure districts over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show an upward trend for at least two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show an upward trend for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains stagnant or declines.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent negative and slightly declining trend in RETAIL_REC over the last four weeks reflects an underlying behavioral shift towards reduced discretionary out-of-home spending and activities, which will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a sustained increase over the next 28 days compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility, plateauing around 7-8% above baseline, indicates a continued behavioral preference for home-based activities, which diverts potential footfall from retail and recreation venues, thereby suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility significantly declines (e.g., below 5%) while RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, rising above the pre-period baseline, would signal a broader return to general out-of-home activity and confidence, providing an immediate positive spillover effect to RETAIL_REC in the very short term.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0% for at least one week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0% for one week, but RETAIL_REC declines in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp seasonal decline in PARKS mobility, combined with the recent upward trend in WORKPLACES mobility, suggests a redirection of out-of-home leisure from outdoor spaces to indoor retail and recreation venues, providing a slight boost to RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week while WORKPLACES increases by at least 1 percentage point.
failure_condition: PARKS declines by more than 2 percentage points and WORKPLACES increases by at least 1 percentage point, but RETAIL_REC continues its downward trend over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The general stagnation or slight decline observed across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL mobility categories indicates a broad and persistent behavioral pattern of reduced overall out-of-home activity, which will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: A significant and sustained increase is observed across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL mobility categories over the next 28 days.
